sources.title: Study on Determining Post-Harvest Losses of Agri-Produces in India
sources.author: NABCONS (NABARD Consultancy Services) for Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)
sources.details: Examined 54 commodities across 84 agro-climatic zones (2020-22). National annual loss Rs 1.53 lakh crore. Fruit losses: 6.02-15.05%, Vegetables: 4.87-11.61%. Tomato total loss 11.62% (8.37% farm level, 3.25% market level). Guava: 15.05%. Discredited the myth of '20% of all produce rots'.

sources.title: Assessment of Quantitative Harvest and Post-Harvest Losses of Major Crops and Commodities in India
sources.author: ICAR-CIPHET (Central Institute of Post-Harvest Engineering and Technology, Ludhiana)
sources.details: Earlier nationwide study documenting post-harvest losses: Fruits 6.70-15.88%, Vegetables 7.32-12.44%.

sources.title: Value Chain Analysis of Processed Tomato in India
sources.author: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit) & MoFPI
sources.details: Processing economics: target raw price Rs 4.5/kg (Rs 450/qtl); mandi typical Rs 6-10/kg crashing to Rs 0.5-2/kg in glut; quality specs TSS 5-6 Brix, acidity >=0.4%, pH <4.5, pulp recovery 40-50%. Processing windows Aug-Oct and Dec-Apr; May-July off-season.

sources.title: Price Volatility and Arrival Dynamics of Tomato in Karnataka APMC Markets
sources.author: Agricultural Economics Research Review
sources.details: Documented weekly price CV of ~77%, arrivals CV of ~102%, and positive price skewness of 2.7. Documented bimodal annual arrivals and shifting seasonal peaks.

sources.title: CEDA Agmarknet Daily Wholesale Prices and Arrivals Data Portal
sources.author: Centre for Economic Data and Analysis (Ashoka University) / Directorate of Marketing & Inspection
sources.details: Historical wholesale prices and arrivals for ~344 commodities and ~4,000 mandis across India from 2001 to present.
